summary: The root "Sfd" primarily means a bond, shackle, or fetter, often used for captives. It also refers to a gift, metaphorically seen as binding the recipient. The plural is "asfād".
lane: صَفَدٌ ذ A bond; (S, K, TA;) as also : (TA:) or, (M, A,) as also , (M,) i. q. , (M, A,) which signifies a rope, (M,) or a thong, (S, K,) or a shackle, or fetter, (S, A, K,) or a [ collar of iron which is put upon the neck or around the neck and hands together, such as is called ] غُلّ , (S, M, A,) with which one is made fast, (M,) or with which a captive is made fast: (S, A, K:) pl. أَصْفَادٌ , [expl. in the S and A and K as signifying shackles, or fetters, ] the only known pl., though of the form of a pl. of pauc. (M.) -b2- Also A gift; (S, M, A, K;) [said to be] so called because he upon whom it is conferred is bound thereby; (Ksh and Bd in xxxviii. 37;) and so : (M:) pl. as above. (L.) One says, الصَّفَدُ صَفَدٌ The gift is a shackle, or fetter. (A.) -b3- And i. q. ثَنَآءٌ [which generally means Praise, eulogy, or commendation; but is said by some to mean also the contr. ]. (M.)
